page: Microsoft Azure D4as_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dav6 family, powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor operating at 3.7 GHz. The configuration includes 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with multithreading enabled at 2 threads per core. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The CPU cache configuration consists of 32 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache. It lacks local storage and GPUs but is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-core performance, with a stress-ng single-core CPU score of 3079.08 and a Geekbench single-core score of 2095.0, both placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core performance is average, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 6154.87 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 4810.0. Memory bandwidth is a notable bottleneck, with read-only small block and large block bandwidths scoring in the bottom 25% at 214.86 GB/sec and 37.99 GB/sec respectively. Software compilation and database operations also show weaker performance, with PassMark database operations scoring in the bottom 25% at 1929.19.

Given its balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and dedicated CPU allocation, the D4as_v6 is qualitatively cost-efficient for general-purpose workloads that do not require high memory bandwidth or local disk storage. It is well-suited for static web serving, where it achieves a throughput of 6.54 GB/sec, and Redis key-value stores, handling 5.9 million SET operations per second. It can also support light text processing and small-scale language model inference, though it is poorly suited for medium-to-large LLM tasks, database-heavy operations, or intensive software compilation.
